messages:
maya: FYI customer 'ClipBox' is seeing repeated 429s during a live demo. They were on the free tier and hammered the embeddings/chat endpoint with ~20 concurrent requests. They want a short-lived uplift so the demo doesn't fail. Logs below.

rate-limit-bot: SYSTEM — response 429 from api.redwood.ai/generate
```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
x-rate-limit-limit: 60/min
x-rate-limit-remaining: 0
x-rate-limit-reset: 1678901234
x-retry-after: 30
content-type: application/json
{ "error": "rate_limit_exceeded" }
```

sam: Got it. Can you paste the curl they used (sanitized keys) and the org ID? Also which model and endpoint (chat/generate/embeddings) — concurrency details matter.

maya: Paste from customer: `curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat -H \"Authorization: Bearer sk-REDACTED\" -d '{"model":"redwood-3b", "messages":[{"role":"user","content":"summarize ..."}]}'`
They said they opened 18 parallel connections from one host during a demo script. Org ID: org-clipbox-7. They also reported a couple of 401s popping up after their dev rotated keys mid-demo.

devon: 2 quick things: 1) free-tier has lower concurrency and per-minute caps; 18 parallel might easily trip short-window limits. 2) mixing rotated keys can lead to transient 401s while cached tokens are still used by clients.

sam: Repro steps we should try: 1) reproduce with a single API key doing N concurrent requests from same IP to mimic demo harness. 2) capture full response headers (x-rate-limit-* and x-retry-after). 3) check logs for `429` vs `401` sequence — if 401 immediately follows a rotation, likely token sync problem.

maya: Customer asks: can we grant a 24h burst so they can finish the demo and convert? They don't have a paid plan yet; would a sales-assisted temporary lift work for free->paid demos?

oliver: Sales here — yes, we can do a short demo uplift. What I need: expected QPS, estimated token spend, and a contact email. We typically provision a 48–72h demo bump (no charge) for high-conversion trials, or a 24h uplift to 2x concurrency for smaller asks. If they plan ongoing usage, we can convert to paid and onboard.

ingrid: Billing note — for free orgs we can authorize a temporary burst if Sales approves and we log an exception. For anything beyond 72h we require card on file or signed order. If they hit platform abuse signals (very high token volume from free signups), we triage separately.

sam: Technical mitigation while we process uplift: add client-side exponential backoff + jitter (retry on 429 with increasing delays), reduce parallel streams to <=8 for demo, and avoid simultaneous key rotation. Also recommend they enable request-level batching (where possible) to reduce per-minute token spikes. Example retry pseudocode: `sleep = base * 2**attempt + rand_between(0, base)` and abort after 5 attempts.

devon: Also check whether their API calls are mixing multiple API keys from the same org in the demo harness. We sometimes see per-key rate limits and per-org safeguards interact; if they used multiple ephemeral keys, that can cause confusing 401/429 patterns.

maya: I'll relay mitigation steps and ask for QPS + token estimate. If sales OKs, we want a 24–72h bump and a clear rollback plan.

sam: Created internal case ID: 2026-4587. @oliver if you approve, I'll attach the monitoring policy and temporary ingress rule so we can increase their per-minute cap to 2x for the window and watch metrics.

oliver: Approve provisional 48h uplift for org-clipbox-7. Sales will follow up with ClipBox contact. Tagging for onboarding checklist. :handshake:

ingrid: Noted — billing will mark exception and confirm end timestamp.

maya: Thanks team — I'll coordinate the demo uplift, send the customer the client-side retry snippet, and ask them to avoid key rotation mid-demo. Will update case 2026-4587 when done.
